o1.biggest_strength: It resurrects the paused front-of-pack winner with fresh words, builds the taste angle straight from the 26% review phrase, and faces the ₹90-a-bar objection head-on, all in blunt brand voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 27-character headline limit is more conservative than Meta's actual ~40, which is fine, but P4 ('Not even a little') repeats a line identical to a live ₹290 ad and is only parked, so the six are slightly less differentiated than claimed.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the price/value angle so it reads as value rather than just repeating the objection, and add per-ad expected lift or kill rules with rupee targets.

o2.biggest_strength: It pairs buyer-phrase headlines and copy (including 'Your 4 pm, minus the samosa') with a real test plan, a control cell, per-cell rupee maths and a 20% win rule that tells you exactly when to act.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents a ₹6,000/day test budget and ties ad C's success to retargeting without brief support, and the early-cut rule (₹1,140 with no purchase) is noisy at these cell sizes.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the invented budget and instead say how to size cells off actual traffic, and make the price ad lead with the ₹90 value rather than quoting the objection.

reason: Both are strong and on-brand; output 2 edges it because its copy sounds more like our customers talking and its launch plan gives me a control, a rupee budget and a clear win rule I can hand to the team tomorrow.
